description: OptimizedMatcher with pooled Order storage vs ReferenceMatcher -- allocation count and latency, same scenario/build type as baseline.json and optimized1.json (Module 12).
method: benchmarks/bench_allocations.cpp: one persistent matcher+OrderManager replays steady_limit_flow across 5 warmup passes (unmeasured, lets the pool's slabs finish growing) then 10 measured passes (200,000 ops), with each pass's order ids offset so a persistent OrderManager doesn't reject repeats as duplicates. Global operator new/delete overridden in that one executable only.

latency_delta_vs_module_12.note: optimized1.json measured p50/p99 on a fresh-matcher-per-iteration harness (bench_match_optimized); this file's harness is a persistent-matcher replay instead, so absolute numbers aren't directly comparable -- only the reference-vs-optimized gap within each file is.

notes: Pooling covers Order object storage only (FixedObjectPool<Order>, include/titan/core/memory_pool.hpp) -- Level::orders (vector<Order*>), the map<Price,Level> node, and the unordered_map<OrderId,OrderRef> node all still allocate at the same rate as ReferenceMatcher. See docs/benchmark-results/allocations.md for the full breakdown of why this isn't closer to zero.
5.4% fewer allocations is modest, not the 'near-zero' language in the module task -- reported as measured, not assumed.
10k-op ReferenceVsOptimized, FuzzMatcherParity, and ItchEngineParityOptimized tests found zero mismatches before these numbers were recorded (151/151 tests passing).
